What to record: Identify the released project, material batch, and cut-list revision.
Record who set up and ran the process plus the production date.
Identify machine, blade, bit, cutter, jig, or program version.
State the face, edge, fence, stop, datum, or coordinate origin.
Example: Show face up / factory left edge

What to record: Record part ID, target dimensions, tolerance, material, and orientation.
Record actual length, width, thickness, diagonals, and critical features.
Inspect edges, faces, grain, damage, label, and handedness.
Example: Pass / A face out / left confirmed

What to record: Record mock assembly, hardware test, disposition, approver, and time.
